triggers: how do I list files
how do I see what's in a folder
how do I navigate directories
how to move around the filesystem
what's the command to list a directory
how do I show hidden files
answer:
Move around and list files with the standard tools:

```
ls            # list the current directory
ls -la        # long form, including hidden (dot) files
cd <dir>      # change directory   (cd ~ = home, cd - = previous)
pwd           # print the directory you're in
```

InterGenOS also ships friendlier viewers: `bat` (a syntax-highlighting `cat`), `eza`-style listings where installed, and `fd` for finding files. For a graphical view, open **Files** (Nautilus).

triggers: how do I copy a file
how do I move a file
how do I rename a file
how do I delete a file
how to remove a directory
what's the command to copy a folder
answer:
Copy, move/rename, and remove with coreutils:

```
cp <src> <dst>           # copy a file   (cp -r for a directory)
mv <src> <dst>           # move OR rename (same command)
rm <file>                # delete a file
rm -r <dir>              # delete a directory and its contents
mkdir <dir>              # make a directory
```

`rm` is permanent — there's no recycle bin on the command line, so double-check the path. Use `rm -i` to be prompted for each file. To delete safely from the desktop, use the **Files** app, which moves to Trash.

triggers: how do I create a file
how do I make a new file
how do I write text to a file
how do I save text into a file
how to create an empty file
what's the command to create a file
answer:
Create a file, or write text into one:

```
touch <file>                 # create an empty file (or refresh its timestamp)
echo 'text' > <file>         # write text, REPLACING the file's contents
echo 'more' >> <file>        # APPEND a line (>> never overwrites)
printf 'a\nb\n' > <file>     # write several lines at once
cat > <file>                 # type lines, then Ctrl-D to save
```

`>` overwrites, `>>` appends — pick carefully. For more than a line or two, open an editor: `nano <file>` (simple, with on-screen key hints) or `vim <file>`. On the desktop, use the **Text Editor** app.

triggers: how do I change file permissions
how do I make a file executable
how do I change the owner of a file
how to fix permission denied
what's the command for chmod
how do I set permissions on a folder
answer:
Permissions and ownership:

```
chmod +x <file>          # make a script executable
chmod 644 <file>         # owner read/write, others read-only
chmod -R 755 <dir>       # recurse into a directory
sudo chown <user> <file>      # change owner (needs sudo)
sudo chown <user>:<group> <file>
```

`ls -l` shows current permissions (the `rwx` columns). A "permission denied" usually means you need `sudo` for a system path, or the file isn't marked executable (`chmod +x`).

triggers: how do I find a file
how do I search for a file by name
how do I search inside files
how to locate a file
what's the command to search file contents
how do I grep for something
answer:
Find files by name and search their contents:

```
find . -name '*.conf'        # files matching a pattern under here
fd conf                      # faster, simpler (ships on InterGenOS)
grep -r 'text' <dir>         # search file CONTENTS recursively
rg 'text'                    # ripgrep — much faster, respects .gitignore
```

`fd` and `rg` (ripgrep) ship by default and are the quick path; `find` and `grep` are always there as the portable fallback.

triggers: how do I read a file
how do I view a file
how do I read a file in linux
how do I see the contents of a file
what's the command to read a file
how do I open a file to read it
answer:
Read or view a file's contents:

```
cat <file>           # print the whole file
bat <file>           # cat with syntax highlighting (ships on InterGenOS)
less <file>          # scroll a long file (q to quit, / to search)
head <file>          # first 10 lines   (head -n 50 for more)
tail <file>          # last 10 lines
tail -f <file>       # follow a log as it grows
```

`cat` for short files, `less` for long ones, `tail -f` to watch a log live. On the desktop, open it in the **Text Editor**.

triggers: how do I find a file by name
answer:
```
fd myfile               # shipped fast finder (packages/base/fd), searches under the current dir
fd -H myfile /          # include hidden files; search from root
# classic equivalent (findutils-core is also shipped):
find / -name 'myfile' 2>/dev/null
```

triggers: where is this file located
answer:
```
fd -H '<filename>' /            # find every path matching that name
# already know it's a command on PATH? locate its binary:
which <command>                # e.g. which python
```

triggers: how do I search for text inside files
answer:
```
rg 'search text'               # ripgrep (packages/base/ripgrep): recursive, respects .gitignore, fast
rg -i 'text'                   # case-insensitive
rg 'text' /etc                 # limit to a directory
# classic fallback (grep-core is shipped):
grep -rn 'text' .
```

triggers: how do I find which file contains a word
answer:
```
rg -l 'word'                   # list only the filenames that contain the word
rg -l 'word' /etc              # scoped to a directory
```

triggers: how do I move a file to another folder
answer:
```
mv file.txt ~/Documents/            # move file.txt into ~/Documents
mv *.png ~/Pictures/                # move all matching files
```

triggers: how do I delete a folder and everything in it
answer:
```
rm -r foldername/                   # recursively delete a folder and its contents
rm -ri foldername/                  # prompt for each item (safer)
```
Note: this is permanent — there is no undo and it does not go to a trash bin.

triggers: how do I create a symlink
answer:
```

```

triggers: how do I extract a tar.gz file
answer:
```
tar -xzf archive.tar.gz             # extract into the current directory
tar -xzf archive.tar.gz -C ~/dest   # extract into ~/dest
# .tar.xz -> -xJf ; .tar.bz2 -> -xjf ; plain .tar -> -xf
```

triggers: how do I unzip a file
answer:
```
unzip archive.zip                   # extract a .zip (provided by bsdunzip -> /usr/bin/unzip)
unzip archive.zip -d ~/dest         # extract into ~/dest
# GUI: open the .zip in Files and choose "Extract" (file-roller).
```
Note: on InterGenOS `unzip` is the libarchive `bsdunzip` engine — same syntax as Info-ZIP for common cases.

triggers: how do I zip a folder
answer:
```
zip -r archive.zip foldername/      # create archive.zip from a folder (packages/base/zip)
# GUI: right-click the folder in Files -> "Compress..." (file-roller).
# Prefer tar+gzip on Linux for full permission/symlink fidelity:
tar -czf archive.tar.gz foldername/
```

triggers: how do I save and quit in vim
answer:
```
Press Esc to leave insert mode, then type:
  :wq   (or :x)   -> save and quit
  :q!             -> quit WITHOUT saving
  :w              -> save without quitting
```

triggers: how do I save and exit nano
answer:

```
Ctrl+O  then Enter   -> write (save) the file
Ctrl+X               -> exit  (nano prompts to save if there are unsaved changes)
```
